newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, China agree to seek fisheries pact.
newsitem.headline: Japan, China agree to seek fisheries pact.

text.p: Agriculture Minister Takao Fujimoto and his Chinese counterpart Liu Jiang will seek a bilateral fisheries accord as soon as possible, a Japanese agriculture ministry official said on Monday.

Talks on a fisheries accord between Tokyo and Beijing have been deadlocked because of Japan's plans for a 200-nautical mile exclusive economic zone, which would encompass a chain of disputed islands in the East China Sea.
Japan, China and Taiwan all claim sovereignty over the islands, known as the Senkaku islands in Japan and Diaoyu islands in China.
Fujimoto and Jiang held a 40-minute meeting in Tokyo on Monday, discussing agricultural and fishing issues between the two countries, the ministry official said.
During the meeting, the Chinese minister said when the two sides will be able to reach a fisheries pact will depend on how serious they are, the Japanese official said.
But the ministers did not directly raise the issue of the disputed islands during the meeting, the official said.
